crm_notes:
Lead source: inbound signup (organic blog + Hacker News mention). Small support-SaaS startup building a chat-first customer support assistant (beta w/ 500 weekly active agents).

Quick firmographics: 15 devs + 6 CS/ops, Series A (pre-revenue ARR ~<$100k), HQ Seattle, US. Tech stack: Node backend, Postgres, AWS us-west-2.

Conversation summary (discovery call 2026-03-02, ff id above):
- Primary user: Head of Product (Maya Ortiz) — wants fast time-to-value and predictable per-message cost.
- Workloads: chat assistant (session-based), embeddings for semantic search, light reranking for ticket suggestions.
- Targets: sub-300ms p50 for short chat responses, p95 <700ms acceptable for now; throughput 150 concurrent sessions initial.
- Cost sensitivity: high — estimate 100M tokens/month at scale but POC focused on ~1M tokens. Wants clear unit economics.
- Models: open to small / mid-sized open models + Redwood verified variants. Interested in quantized variants if latency/cost tradeoff is good.
- Routing/fallback: want hosted API but asked about automatic fallback to cheaper variant during spikes.

Security / compliance conversation:
- Needs SSO/SAML for staff console (not for end-users). SOC2 compliance desirable — wants audit logging and simple retention controls. Data residency not required yet.

Procurement / billing notes (key subject):
- Team prefers CC for self-serve, but finance asked about invoice terms for monthly billing once over ~$3k/mo.
- Startup discount requested (they have YC-style program in past) — asked if Redwood offers credits or startup partner program.
- POC ask: extend free credits (current free tier used up) for 60 days to finish integration and run load test.
- Quote: quick estimate provided in Drive pricing_deck_sunseed_v1.pdf (link above).

Timeline & recent activities:
- 2026-02-20: inbound signup, trial keys issued (no CC on file).
- 2026-02-25: automated usage spike -> rate limit hit, customer pinged support. (JIRA-6127 opened).
- 2026-03-02: discovery call w/ Jordan, Priya joined for technical Qs (ff meeting).
- 2026-03-05: follow-up email with pricing summary and integration notes (gthreaded id).
- 2026-03-09: customer requested formal invoice option and startup discount details.

Requirements checklist (POC):
- Hosted API access with token/role separation (dev vs prod keys).
- Rate limits flexible for POC (temporary higher quota).
- Quickstart SDKs for Node + Python.
- Billing: temporary CC preferred, but need options for invoice at ~30d net once ARR grows.
- Support: dev office hours + one scheduled deep-dive with SE on model tuning and batching.

Quoted next steps (short):
- Jordan to confirm whether finance will accept CC for POC or insist on invoice (due by 2026-03-13).
- Redwood to propose 60-day free credit extension + outline startup discount criteria (deliver by 2026-03-12).
- Priya to schedule technical deep-dive (agenda: batching, KV caching, latency tuning) for week of 2026-03-15.

Notes / quotes from Maya: "We want an API that behaves predictably under load and a clear path to lower per-token cost — but we need to get through procurement without months of paperwork. If we can sign via CC and then convert later, that keeps velocity."

Open items / blockers (short):
- Finance needs vendor paperwork for invoice path (simple W-9 + PO process).
- Confirm eligibility for startup discount (proofs requested).
- Provide formal POC extension note for internal approval.

Suggested AE play: keep it self-serve friendly, do short-term CC for velocity + provide a neat invoice path doc and checklist (templates), grant 60-day credits to finish POC, follow with a low-friction transition to monthly invoice once spend exceeds threshold.
